source_text: Non ergo sine adiutorio Dei ad cultum eius, qualem exhibent initiati mysteriis, liberum arbitrium idoneum credimus, sed divinae aequitatis locupletem testem libertatem arbitrii confitemur, ut eo tempore, quo nos manifestari oportet ante tribunal Christi et recipere unumquemque propria corporis sicut gessit, sive bonum sive malum, nihil Deus iniuste iudicare doceatur, qui nulli imputat peccatum, nisi quod is, qui propter illud ponitur, potuit et cavere.
pass_a_gloss: Not therefore without the help of God do we believe free choice suitable to his worship such as the initiated in mysteries exhibit, but we confess the liberty of choice a wealthy witness of divine fairness, that at that time when it is necessary we be manifested before the tribunal of Christ and each receive the proper things of the body as he has carried, whether good or evil, God be taught to judge nothing unjustly, who imputes to no one a sin except that which he who is placed on account of it could also have beenware.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: We do not, then, believe that free will without God’s help is adequate for the worship offered by those initiated into the sacred mysteries. Rather, we acknowledge freedom of choice as a fully competent witness to divine fairness. When we must appear before Christ’s judgment seat and each receive what belongs to deeds done in the body, whether good or evil (2 Corinthians 5:10), God will be shown to judge nothing unjustly: he charges no one with a sin unless the person punished for it could also have avoided it.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Appearance before Christ’s judgment seat and repayment for bodily deeds.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
